   1. The abacus originated in ancient Mesopotamia around two thousand five hundred years ago. This simple counting frame used beads sliding on rods to perform basic arithmetic operations. Merchants and scholars relied on this mechanical tool for centuries before modern calculators existed.
   *(3 sentences. Good.)*

   2. The Antikythera mechanism represents an extraordinary ancient Greek analog computer. Archaeologists discovered this bronze device inside a shipwreck near a small Greek island. Its intricate gear system predicted astronomical positions and eclipses with remarkable precision.
   *(3 sentences. Good.)*

   3. Blaise Pascal invented the first mechanical calculator in sixteen forty-two. He designed this device to help his father calculate taxes more efficiently. The Pascaline could add and subtract directly through a series of carefully engineered wheels.
   *(3 sentences. Good.)*

   4. Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz expanded upon earlier mechanical designs by creating the stepped reckoner. This innovative machine introduced a drum mechanism that enabled multiplication and division. Leibniz also championed the binary number system that would later revolutionize digital electronics
